elements.label: Figure 1
elements.title: Total external debt, 2015–25
elements.description: The chart shows Tonga's total external debt from 2015 to 2025. Debt fluctuated, reaching a high around 2021 before falling to 164.1 in 2025.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 2
elements.title: External debt by creditor and creditor type in 2025, including IMF credit and SDR allocations

data.label: Public & publicly guaranteed - by creditor type

elements.description: The graphic breaks down 2025 external debt by creditor type and creditor. All 164.1 million is public and publicly guaranteed, comprising 111.5 million multilateral and 52.6 million bilateral debt. China accounts for all bilateral debt; among the displayed individual multilateral categories, World Bank-IDA is largest and IMF-SDR allocations are smallest.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 3
elements.title: Debt ratios, 2015–25
legend: 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries (shaded band)
elements.description: Four panels show external debt and debt service relative to exports and GNI from 2015 to 2025. The displayed 2025 ratios are highest for external debt / exports at 83% and lowest for debt service / GNI at 3%. All four displayed changes are negative.
elements.notes: Shaded band shows the 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries. Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 4
elements.title: Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025
elements.description: Two side-by-side boxes show official creditors and private creditors. Each box lists maturity, grace period and interest rate, all marked '..'. No values are shown because Tonga had no new commitments in 2025.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database. Note: Figure 4 shows no data values for official or private creditors because the country did not have new commitments in 2025.
